title: Rigveda 2.41: Diverse gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 2.41: Diverse gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 2.41 is a hymn of 21 verses addressed to diverse gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 2, the family book of Gṛtsamada. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 181v-182v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 2.41.1-3 (aṣṭaka 2, adhyāya 8, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 181v
translation.original_text:
1vāyo̱ ye te̍ saha̱sriṇo̱ rathā̍sa̱s tebhi̱r ā ga̍hi | ni̱yutvā̱n soma̍pītaye ||
2ni̱yutvā̍n vāya̱v ā ga̍hy a̱yaṁ śu̱kro a̍yāmi te | gantā̍si sunva̱to gṛ̱ham ||
3śu̱krasyā̱dya gavā̍śira̱ indra̍vāyū ni̱yutva̍taḥ | ā yā̍ta̱m piba̍taṁ narā ||
translation.text:
1O Vâyu, come to us with all the thousand chariots that are thine, Team-borne, to drink the Soma juice.
2Drawn by thy team, O Vâyu, come; to thee is offered this, the pure. Thou visitest the presser's house.
3Indra and Vâyu, drawn by teams, ye Heroes, come today and drink. Of the bright juice when blent with milk.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 181v (numbered 3v by the scribe) (OPenn image 183, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 2.40.3 ‹rajasaḥ vi-mānam sapta-cakram ratham›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 182r (numbered 4r by the scribe), begins in RV 2.41.4 ‹-mama it iha śratam›. Verses 2.41.1-3 end on this page.

3śukrasya | adya | go--āśiraḥ | indravāyūiti | niyutvataḥ | ā | yātam | pibatam | narā

translation.original_ref: RV 2.41.4-17 (aṣṭaka 2, adhyāya 8, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 182r
translation.original_text:
4a̱yaṁ vā̍m mitrāvaruṇā su̱taḥ soma̍ ṛtāvṛdhā | mamed i̱ha śru̍ta̱ṁ hava̍m ||
5rājā̍nā̱v ana̍bhidruhā dhru̱ve sada̍sy utta̱me | sa̱hasra̍sthūṇa āsāte ||
6tā sa̱mrājā̍ ghṛ̱tāsu̍tī ādi̱tyā dānu̍na̱s patī̍ | sace̍te̱ ana̍vahvaram ||
7goma̍d ū̱ ṣu nā̍sa̱tyāśvā̍vad yātam aśvinā | va̱rtī ru̍drā nṛ̱pāyya̍m ||
8na yat paro̱ nānta̍ra āda̱dharṣa̍d vṛṣaṇvasū | du̱ḥśaṁso̱ martyo̍ ri̱puḥ ||
9tā na̱ ā vo̍ḻham aśvinā ra̱yim pi̱śaṅga̍saṁdṛśam | dhiṣṇyā̍ varivo̱vida̍m ||
10indro̍ a̱ṅga ma̱had bha̱yam a̱bhī ṣad apa̍ cucyavat | sa hi sthi̱ro vica̍rṣaṇiḥ ||
11indra̍ś ca mṛ̱ḻayā̍ti no̱ na na̍ḥ pa̱ścād a̱ghaṁ na̍śat | bha̱dram bha̍vāti naḥ pu̱raḥ ||
12indra̱ āśā̍bhya̱s pari̱ sarvā̍bhyo̱ abha̍yaṁ karat | jetā̱ śatrū̱n vica̍rṣaṇiḥ ||
13viśve̍ devāsa̱ ā ga̍ta śṛṇu̱tā ma̍ i̱maṁ hava̍m | edam ba̱rhir ni ṣī̍data ||
14tī̱vro vo̱ madhu̍mām̐ a̱yaṁ śu̱naho̍treṣu matsa̱raḥ | e̱tam pi̍bata̱ kāmya̍m ||
15indra̍jyeṣṭhā̱ maru̍dgaṇā̱ devā̍sa̱ḥ pūṣa̍rātayaḥ | viśve̱ mama̍ śrutā̱ hava̍m ||
16ambi̍tame̱ nadī̍tame̱ devi̍tame̱ sara̍svati | a̱pra̱śa̱stā i̍va smasi̱ praśa̍stim amba nas kṛdhi ||
17tve viśvā̍ sarasvati śri̱tāyū̍ṁṣi de̱vyām | śu̱naho̍treṣu matsva pra̱jāṁ de̍vi didiḍḍhi naḥ ||
translation.text:
4This Soma hath been shed for you, Lawstrengtheners, Mitra-Varuṇa! Listen ye here to this my call.
5Both Kings who never injure aught seat them in their supremest home, The thousand-pillared, firmly-based.
6Fed with oblation, Sovran Kings, Âdityas, Lords of liberal gifts. They wait on him whose life is true.
7With kine, Nâsatyas, and with steeds, come, Aṣvins, Rudras, to the house That will protect its heroes well;
8Such, wealthy Gods! as none afar nor standing nigh to us may harm, Yea, no malicious mortal foe.
9As such, O longed-for Aṣvins, lead us on to wealth of varied sort, Wealth that shall bring us room and rest.
10Verily Indra, conquering all, driveth e'en mighty fear away, For firm is he and swift to act.
11Indra be gracious unto us: sin shall not reach us afterward, And good shall be before us still.
12From all the regions of the world let Indra send security, The foe-subduer, swift to act.
13O all ye Gods, come hitherward: hear this mine invocation, seat Yourselves upon this sacred grass.
14Among the Ṣunahotras strong for you is this sweet gladdening draught. Drink ye of this delightsome juice.
15Ye Martus led by Indra, Gods with Pri§an for your bounteousest, Hear all of you this call of mine.
16Best Mother, best of Rivers, best of Goddesses, Sarasvatî, We are, as 'twere, of no repute and dear Mother, give thou us renown.
17In thee, Sarasvatî, divine, all generations have their stay. Be, glad with Ṣunahotra's sons: O Goddess grant us progeny.

translation.original_ref: RV 2.41.18-21 (aṣṭaka 2, adhyāya 8, varga 10); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 182v
translation.original_text:
18i̱mā brahma̍ sarasvati ju̱ṣasva̍ vājinīvati | yā te̱ manma̍ gṛtsama̱dā ṛ̍tāvari pri̱yā de̱veṣu̱ juhva̍ti ||
19pretā̍ṁ ya̱jñasya̍ śa̱mbhuvā̍ yu̱vām id ā vṛ̍ṇīmahe | a̱gniṁ ca̍ havya̱vāha̍nam ||
20dyāvā̍ naḥ pṛthi̱vī i̱maṁ si̱dhram a̱dya di̍vi̱spṛśa̍m | ya̱jñaṁ de̱veṣu̍ yacchatām ||
21ā vā̍m u̱pastha̍m adruhā de̱vāḥ sī̍dantu ya̱jñiyā̍ḥ | i̱hādya soma̍pītaye ||
translation.text:
18Enriched with sacrifice, accept Sarasvatî, these prayers of ours, Thoughts which Gr̥itsamadas beloved of Gods bring, Holy One,to thee.
19Ye who bless sacrifice, go forth, for verily we choose you both, And Agni who conveys our gifts.
20This our.effectual sacrifice, reaching the sky, shall Heaven and Earth Present unto the Gods to-day.
21In both your laps, ye guileless Ones, the Holy Gods shall sit them down To-day to drink the Soma here.
